latest_release.name: SolidCraft v0.41.0
latest_release.body:
**0.41.0 brings the first version of plugins, makes fillets and STEP imports hold up on real parts, keeps sheet-metal folds from shattering into strips, and adds Blender-style trackpad input and a Constrain dialog for assemblies.**

SolidCraft is open-source parametric 3D CAD in Rust: sketch, constrain, extrude, and change a parameter to watch the timeline rebuild. [Website](https://solidcraft.io) · [documentation](https://docs.solidcraft.io/) · [Discord](https://solidcraft.io/discord) · [issues](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/issues).

0.41.0 is a minor release: it adds new features and writes a new design file format (see Compatibility). It goes out as a pre-release first.

## New
- **Plugins, first version.** SolidCraft can run sandboxed WebAssembly plugins. A plugin works only through SolidCraft's own commands, the same ones scripts and AI agents use, and only with the permissions you grant. It has no network access, and fuel and memory limits stop a runaway plugin. One plugin run is one undo step. The plugin API is `craft:plugin@0.1.0`. This first version is experimental (#15112).
- **Install a plugin from its .zip** with Install plugin… in Preferences › Plugins or the Plugins menu. It shows what the plugin asks for before installing (#15644).
- **A Plugins menu** runs installed plugins; each one gets a dialog built from its parameters (#15673).
- The first plugin is out: [SolidCraft Gears](https://github.com/bherbruck/solidcraft-gears), an involute gear generator. Download its .zip from its releases and install it in Preferences › Plugins.
- **Assemblies: a Constrain dialog.** Pick a face, edge, point, plane or axis on each of two parts and place one against the other by a rule such as Mate, Flush or Distance. The dialog offers only the rules your picks fit, lists the constraints already between the two parts, and lets you edit, suppress or delete them (#15146).
- **Split Face along closed shapes.** A new Loops option joins a sketch's curves end to end, so a closed outline of lines and arcs splits the face along that outline only (#15225, #15252).
- **Snap points everywhere.** Construct Point, Axis and Plane, sketch tools, joints and the placement point of Box, Sphere and Torus take the centre, middle or end of an edge, face or sketch curve; construction follows it when the model changes (#11233, #11234, #11232, #11235).
- **Blender-style trackpad input:** in the Blender navigation preset, two fingers on a trackpad orbit and Shift + two fingers pan, as in Blender (#15188). A new opt-in setting lets you twist two fingers to turn the view about the up axis (#12737).
- **GLB export keeps an assembly's structure:** each component and occurrence is its own named, movable node (#15662).
- **Sketch dimension text** takes a size and colour preference (#14304).
- **Reopening a STEP file** reuses your earlier answer to "wrong way up?" instead of asking again (#8630).
- **Spline tangent handles** at every fit point of a spline (#6511).
- **Joint symbols:** an option on the Graphics page draws a badge for each joint type, which goes quiet once the joint's parts can't move (#10668).
- **Threads:** the ISO metric sizes that were missing, such as M3.5, M7, M33, M39 and M45 (#5128).
- **Sheet metal:** contour flanges accept tangent arcs (#15287).
- **Split Body** by a closed surface such as a sphere (#14214).
- **One docking system for Design and Render.** Panels dock the same way in both workspaces, and Preferences no longer offers a choice between docking systems. Saved panel layouts still work, the Classic layout is still available as an arrangement, and editors such as Extrude open as cards you can drag (#15184).
- **Save shows its progress** and can be cancelled until the file is replaced (#9560).
- Document tabs show the saved file name, and the window title shows the design and whether it has unsaved changes (#7298, #14833).
- The app shows that it is starting while it loads (#3444).
- Project dialog: double-click a

detail.readme:
SolidCraft

An open-source parametric 3D CAD application built in pure Rust.
Sketch, constrain, and build solids with a parametric feature timeline. Change a dimension and watch your model rebuild. Run it on your desktop, in your browser, or let AI agents model through the built-in MCP server.

[![Download for Windows][badge-windows]][windows-msi] [![Download for macOS][badge-macos]][macos-dmg] [![Download for Linux][badge-linux]][linux-appimage] [![Get it from the Snap Store][badge-snap]][snap-store] [![Try it in your browser][badge-web]][web-app]

Website · Download · Try it in the browser · Documentation · Discord · SolidCore

![SolidCraft: model a Raspberry Pi 4 case from an empty design: a sketch dimensioned with parameters, extrude, fillets and shell, a rim rounded in one pick, standoffs patterned on the board's mounting holes, port cut-outs, vent slots, "Pi 4" engraved in a font, a PETG material with its mass in Properties, and a height change in Parameters](docs/screenshots/demo.gif) *A Raspberry Pi 4 case from an empty design: a sketch dimensioned with the board's parameters, extrude, fillet, shell, the rim rounded in one pick, an M2.5 standoff patterned on the 58 × 49 mm hole rectangle, port cut-outs, vent slots, "Pi 4" engraved in DejaVu Sans Bold and a PETG material defined in the design, with its mass in Properties, then height 24 → 32 mm in Parameters and it all rebuilds. 6× playback with the idle pauses cut. [Full video](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/raw/refs/heads/main/docs/screenshots/demo.mp4), recorded with the [demo script](examples/demo/record_ui.sh).* ## Download - **Windows:** the [installer][windows-msi]. - **macOS:** the [disk image][macos-dmg] (Apple silicon and Intel). - **Linux:** the [AppImage][linux-appimage], or `sudo snap install solidcraft` ([Snap Store][snap-store]). - **Web:** [try it in your browser][web-app], no install. ARM64 and 32-bit builds, portable zip, .deb, .rpm, Flatpak and the other packages are on the [downloads page](docs/downloads.md). The macOS app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Windows signing: free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation ([code signing policy](https://docs.solidcraft.io/code-signing-policy.html)). Until the production certificate is in place, SmartScreen may warn: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. On SolidCraft 0.11 to 0.14, download once by hand; see [updating](https://docs.solidcraft.io/guide/updates.html#updating-from-011-to-014). ## What works Early but usable for simple parts: 75 of 76 public reference parts match their analytic or FreeCAD-computed volume, area, centre of mass and bounding box ([oracle](docs/oracle.md)); the other is a tracked bug. - **Sketches and constraints:** lines, arcs, splines, text and more, solved by our own constraint solver, with parameter-driven dimensions. - **Features:** extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, fillet, chamfer, shell, draft, holes, threads, patterns, mirror, split and combine on an editable parametric timeline. - **Parameters and configurations** with unit-aware expressions. - **Assemblies** with joints, motion studies, contact sets, interference and mass properties. - **Sheet metal** with flanges, hems, fold/unfold and flat patterns, and plastic enclosure features. - **Files:** STEP, IGES, 3MF, STL, OBJ and glTF in and out where supported, URDF export, `.sc` designs (`.solidcraft` files from earlier releases still open). - **Desktop app, browser app, headless CLI and MCP server**, all running the same commands. The full list is in [docs/capabilities.md](docs/capabilities.md) and [docs/features.md](docs/features.md); status and plans are in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). See also [what people built](docs/showcase.md), [3D mouse support](docs/3d-mouse.md) and the [architecture](docs/architecture.md). ## Build from source ```sh cargo run --release -p solidcraft -- --sample # desktop app with a sample part cargo run --release -p solidcraft-cli -- commands # the command registry cargo run --release -p solidcraft-cli -- run examples/bracket.json --out bracket.step cargo xtask ci # fmt, clippy, tests, icons, assets, layers, wasm ``` More commands, the Windows cross-build and the browser build are in [docs/building.md](docs/building.md). ## AI agents (MCP) `solidcraft-cli mcp` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Headless it runs its own design session, or with `--connect` it drives the running app so you can watch. Claude Code: `claude mcp add solidcraft -- solidcraft-cli mcp`. If a terminal doesn't find `solidcraft-cli` (older Windows installers don't put it on `PATH`), give its full path (by default `"C:\\Program Files\\SolidCraft\\solidcraft-cli.exe"`). Tools, access rules and an example session: [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md). ## Scripts A script is a JSON list of the same commands the UI runs, executed with `solidcraft-cli run`. Format and example: [docs/scripts.md](docs/scripts.md). Pages can also be driven through the [browser command API](docs/browser-api.md). ## Plugins (experimental desktop runtime) Plugins add separately distributed behaviour without compiling that behaviour into SolidCraft. The initial runtime loads **WebAssembly components**, explicitly requested by the user. Merely installing a folder, enabling it in Preferences, or opening a design never executes plugin code. The interface is experimental: WIT package `craft:plugin@0.1.0`, capability `commands@0.1`. While it is 0.x a minor version may break the one before it; the host refuses a plugin that needs a capability it does not have, in plain words. Review a plugin again after an update. The desktop app and headless CLI use the same commands. Browser execution, automatic downloads and updates, custom panels, and plugin-defined parametric feature types are future work. ### Install and inspect A package is a folder named after its id, containing `plugin.json` and a `.wasm` component. Preferences > Plugins lists packages under the per-user data folder: `%LOCALAPPDATA%/SolidCraft/plugins` on Windows, `~/Library/Application Support/SolidCraft/plugins` on macOS, and `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/solidcraft/plugins` on Linux. **Show in folder** opens this location. You can also inspect and explicitly run a package in another folder. Nothing is downloaded by the host. A minimal manifest looks like this. Plugin packages and examples are maintained outside this repository, as specified in [the plugin RFC](docs/rfcs/0002-plugins.md). ```json { "id": "example-box", "name": "Example box", "version": "0.1.0", "description": "Create an ordinary editable box from dimensions.", "capabilities": ["commands@0.1"], "runtime": { "module": "plugin.wasm", "entries": ["make"], "commands": ["solid.box"], "limits": {"fuel": 10000000, "memory_mib": 64, "deadline_ms": 5000} } } ``` Run `plugin.inspect` with `{"path":"/path/to/example-box"}` through the CLI's JSON scripts, MCP `execute`, or the desktop control channel's `engine.execute`. It reads the manifest and component without executing them, returning the declared commands, limits and an `approval` SHA-256 hash. Review the author, code and declared rights before using that hash. Inspection does not approve a package. Existing metadata-only packages remain listable but cannot run until they declare a runtime. ### Run explicitly After reviewing the inspected package, execute: ```json { "command": "plugin.run", "params": { "path": "/path/to/example-box", "approval": "", "entry": "make", "params": {"length": 20, "width": 10, "height": 3} } } ``` For example, save that command in a JSON array and use `solidcraft-cli run commands.json`. For the running desktop app, send it as the `command` and `params` of a standalone `engine.execute` request (see [control protocol](docs/control-protocol.md)). The native host runs it on a worker and keeps the window responsive. Stop or a design change discards the pending result; the host does not automatically rerun external code. Desktop batches and scripts must send `plugin.run` separately. Headless CLI scripts may include it as a normal command. The hash binds **both the exact manifest bytes and the component bytes**, so an updated package requires a fresh inspection and permission review. It is a content identity, not a signature or an author's reputation. Agent chat asks before executing external plugin code. MCP and the control channel keep their existing file scopes: allow the package folder explicitly where needed. Naming a package never grants access to another folder. ### User resource ceilings The invocation defaults remain **10,000,000 fuel, 64 MiB of guest memory and 5000 ms**. The default host ceilings remain **100,000,000,000 fuel and 128 MiB**. A package can declare larger fuel or memory budgets, but execution is refused until you explicitly raise the host ceilings and approve that exact package content. `plugin.inspect` is inert and reports the requested limits, current `host_limits`, `within_host_limits` and any `limits_error` even when a request is too large. In the native GUI, open **Preferences > Plugins**, enter **Max plugin fuel** and **Max plugin memory (MiB)**, then choose **Apply** or **OK**. Enter also accepts both values; **Cancel** reverts changes since the last Apply and **Restore defaults** resets this page. The settings persist in your user preferences and do not travel with saved designs. For standalone CLI or headless MCP sessions, create a UTF-8 JSON file, for example `plugin-limits.json` containing: ```json {"max_fuel": 200000000000, "max_memory_mib": 512} ``` Pass it explicitly when starting the process: ```text solidcraft-cli --plugin-limits plugin-limits.json run inspect-plugin.json --results solidcraft-cli --plugin-limits plugin-limits.json mcp --headless --allow-path /path/to/plugins ``` Missing fields use the original host ceilings. Connected desktop sessions use the GUI's preferences; CLI settings cannot override them. Positive integer fuel values up to `u64::MAX` are accepted without rounding. Guest memory is limited to 4096 MiB by the current Wasm32 ABI; that technical boundary requires a different runtime ABI to change. Neither setting changes a package's declared budget, executes it, adds permissions, or retries a failed invocation. Review its manifest and component, obtain the content approval hash, and explicitly invoke it. A changed manifest budget requires a fresh approval hash. Keep the selected ceilings within your machine's available resources; they are limits on guest execution, not total SolidCraft memory or native CAD work. The independent maximum execution deadline stays 30 seconds. ### Permissions, results and saved designs A plugin can call any command in the MCP catalog whose exact id its manifest lists. Commands that reach past the open design are grouped: `file` (saving, exporting, importing, inserting from files, libraries), `doc` (opening or switching designs), `app` (settings, window, diagnostics) and `plugin` (inspecting or running plugins). Each group is refused unless the manifest requests it in `runtime.permissions.command_groups` and the user grants it; this version has no grant UI yet. Filesystem calls require matching manifest permissions and approved folder grants. The clock requires its manifest permission; otherwise it returns a fixed epoch. No WASI, socket or process API is linked. A design container reserves `plugins//` for a plugin's own data, kept and saved back untouched when the plugin is missing; plugins cannot read or write it until the `storage` capability arrives. Inspection commands can disclose model data, so review them as permissions too. In particular, the optional `model.mesh` permission exposes the requested body's evaluated vertices and triangles in its owning component's coordinates (millimetres), with explicit transfer limits. It performs no conversion. Edits run against an isolated copy of the design. Only a successful call is adopted, as **one Undo step**. A trap, exhausted fuel, memory limit, invalid result or refused host call discards the transaction, preserving the previous design and undo/redo history. The host validates produced native features before accepting them. A plugin that catches a refused host call cannot commit an earlier partial edit. CPU-heavy guest loops are bounded by fuel and a deadline; the guide explains the separate cost of compiling a component and executing a granted native command. The result is ordinary native features: they save, undo, redo and rebuild without the plugin. Removing the package disables future invocations; it does not remove the features already created. Changing the plugin's own parameters means another invocation in this first version; there is no plugin-owned timeline evaluation hook yet. Turn an installed plugin off in Preferences > Plugins to refuse subsequent desktop calls. Disabling it or changing resource ceilings during a pending call prevents adoption. CLI processes have their own session policy and do not read the desktop app's preferences. See the [runtime and author guide](docs/plugin-runtime.md) for the complete manifest, supported command boundary, limits, build options, tests and current restrictions. For step-by-step package checks and expected results, see the [English test guide](docs/plugin-test-guide.md). The existing [parametric plugin design](docs/plugins.md) remains a separate future phase. ## Contributing Help is welcome. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) covers how to build and test, the code map, the clean-room and licence rules, and where help is wanted most. Open work is in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/issues); chat is on [Discord](https://discord.gg/FtU4NQNVDH). ## Sponsors [![CI powered by Blacksmith](docs/sponsors/blacksmith-ci-powered.png)](https://www.blacksmith.sh) SolidCraft's continuous integration runs on [Blacksmith](https://www.blacksmith.sh), which sponsors its CI minutes. ## Disclaimer The files in this repository are provided as is, without warranty, liability or indemnity, and Tangency Labs and the contributors accept no responsibility for any harmful or unlawful use of them: read [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md). ## Licence MIT OR Apache-2.0, at your option.
